risks.note: The company swung from a pre-exceptional loss in the prior year to only a marginal profit before tax in 2025-26, and the turnaround rests on operational efficiencies, cost management, business mix and working capital optimisation rather than structural pricing power. Directors did not recommend any dividend for FY2026, citing current year performance and future growth needs.
risks.risk: Thin, volatile profitability with limited buffer

risks.note: Revenue sits almost entirely in Products & Solutions (PSG) and Customer Support Services (CSS). PSG, the larger contributor, grew only ~3% versus 13% for CSS, so overall growth depends disproportionately on the services segment while the product business remains the bigger but slower base.
risks.risk: Concentration in two segments, with the larger one growing slowly

risks.note: CSS growth is attributed to deeper engagement with key customers and the addition of new service engagements, and EMS scale-up depends on manufacturing orders secured from 'strategic customers'. Loss or non-renewal of a small number of anchor relationships would be material to both segments.
risks.risk: Dependence on a few key customers and service engagements

risks.note: Electronic Manufacturing Services, Infrastructure Management Services and Green Energy are described as new growth areas being invested in, with EMS only 'laying a strong foundation for scaling up in the coming years'. Returns are back-ended and none of these has yet demonstrated scale or profitability.
risks.risk: Execution risk in unproven new growth verticals

risks.note: The IMS/CSS business runs customer infrastructure across endpoints, data centres and cloud with a stated 99.99% availability commitment, NOC/SOC operations and 100% security patch compliance. The company itself flags 'evolving cybersecurity threats'; a breach or sustained availability failure at a client would carry direct contractual and reputational consequences.
risks.risk: Cybersecurity and service-availability exposure in managed services

risks.note: With a 1000+ employee base and delivery through field engineers, service partners and engineering staff, the business model is labour-led. Management explicitly frames workforce attraction and retention (competitive compensation, career pathways, feedback mechanisms) as a critical enabler of sustained performance, making attrition a structural, not incidental, risk.
risks.risk: People-intensive model dependent on attracting and retaining talent

risks.note: Strategy calls for investment in manufacturing infrastructure, assembly capabilities and PCB production to raise local value addition and compete for government and institutional opportunities. This shifts a historically asset-light distributor/service company toward fixed-cost manufacturing, raising operating leverage and utilisation risk.

The cautionary statement expressly notes that actual outcomes on growth strategy, financial performance, product potential and development initiatives may differ materially from stated expectations, and that the company undertakes no obligation to update them.
risks.risk: Forward-looking growth plans subject to material variance
